title: Entergy Louisiana invests in the future workforce through STEM scholarships for students attending Historically Black Colleges and Universities
summary: Entergy Louisiana is investing in the future of higher education and workforce development by awarding $35,000 in STEM scholarships to nine students attending Historically Black Colleges and…
body_markdown:
BATON ROUGE – Entergy Louisiana is investing in the future of higher education and workforce development by awarding $35,000 in STEM scholarships to nine students attending Historically Black Colleges and Universities, or HBCUs, and partner institutions across Louisiana. The scholarships are part of Entergy’s $20 Million Power of Prosperity initiative, which supports HBCUs and minority-serving institutions across the Gulf South to help remove barriers to students’ academic success.


The initiative pillars include academic scholarships, workforce development including student internships, mentoring and faculty externships; generational wealth-building; and competitive facility grants and endowments. Scholarships are awarded to students pursuing degrees in high-demand fields such as computer science, information technology, engineering and related disciplines that align with the evolving energy workforce.


“These students represent the future of our communities across the Gulf South region. Their talent, determination and ambition will help shape the next generation of innovation, industry and economic development across our state,” said Phillip May, president & CEO of Entergy Louisiana. “By investing in their education today, we’re not only opening doors of opportunity, we’re building a stronger, more resilient workforce that will support our communities for years to come.”


The Competitive Facilities Grant portion of the program will provide up to $1 million in funding this year for accredited HBCUs and Minority Serving Institutions in Entergy’s service area to help upgrade classrooms, labs and equipment. Awards will be announced during the fall semester.


The 2026 scholarship recipients are:


**Nana Akwasi Owusu** | Grambling State University | Computer Science


**Trevoris Norman Jr** | Baton Rouge Community College | Chemical Process Technology


**Amos Cravins** | Baton Rouge Community College | Chemical Process Technology


**Bennie Ferguson** | Grambling State University | Computer Science


**Patrick Bofah** | Grambling State University | Computer Science


**Eniola Irinoye** | Grambling State University | Electrical/Electronic Engineering Technology


**Jean Bordelon** | Baton Rouge Community College | Chemical Process Technology


**Metherbe Ncube** | Grambling State University | Computer Science


**Jarkiya Boudreaux** | Baton Rouge Community College | Chemical Process Technology ****


[Learn more here](https://www.entergy.com/news/entergy-makes-20m-commitment-empower-historically-black-colleges-universities-students) about Entergy’s Power of Prosperity program.


**About Entergy Louisiana**


Entergy Louisiana provides electricity to more than 1.1 million customers in 58 parishes. Entergy Louisiana is a subsidiary of Entergy Corporation (NYSE: ETR). Entergy generates, transmits and distributes electricity to power life for 3 million customers through our operating companies in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas. We’re focused on keeping costs for our customers as low as possible while providing reliable energy that our communities count on. We’re also investing in growth for the future with a more resilient, cleaner energy system that includes modern natural gas, nuclear and renewable energy generation. As a nationally recognized leader in sustainability and corporate citizenship, Entergy delivers more than $100 million in economic benefits each year to the communities we serve through philanthropy, volunteerism and advocacy. Entergy is a Fortune 500 company headquartered in New Orleans, Louisiana, and has approximately 12,000 employees.
